Commentary.Commentary: That's all from England, they lose their last four wickets for only 10 runs and have set a target of 170 runs in front of the Aussies. We sensed a momentum shift after the tea break when the pair of Moeen Ali and Jonny Bairstow started to counterattack. Soon, Steven Smith was put on the defensive which was evident from his field placement. But a rather debatable decision against Moeen Ali opened the floodgates. The English lower order just failed to withstand the short pitch stuff from the Aussies and surrendered meekly. Tea has been taken and we will join you on the other side with Australia's reply.

OUT! That is it! Australia have blown the tail away here. A barrage of short balls have done the job. Cummins comes steaming in and bangs it short, a well-directed one. Ball has taken his eyes off the ball as he tries to fend at it. It takes the edge of the bat and flies over the slip cordon. Handscomb moves across to his left from fly slip and completes another catch. Brilliant end to the session for the home side as ENGLAND HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 195!
Once again Pat tests the number 11 with a bumper. Ball is evading it safely.
Another bouncer, Cummins is at the batsman here. Ball ducks underneath it.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Pat Cummins is into the attack.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
James Anderson is the last man in.

OUT! Successful review by the Australians! Tim Paine, you beauty, he was spot on with his appeal. Smart bowling by Starc and he has got his revenge. He was bowling it short and now suddenly dishes out a full ball which angles across the batsman. Broad was not expecting this and he tries to defend the ball from within his crease. The ball goes off something to the keeper who appeals. He is the only one appealing there as Starc is not interested. Tim convinces his captain to take a review. They go upstairs. Replays roll in and Hot Spot was not that conclusive at first but there is some spike as the ball passes the bat on Snicko and the on-field call has to be changed. Broad is walking back and he is not happy about it, as he feels he has not edged it. Later on, Ultra Edge shows there is a mark as the ball passes the bat. An excellent review and England are 9 down.
Review time! Starc is not confident but Paine surely is. He feels that Broad has edged it and they have gone upstairs against Broad who has played back to a very full ball.
The ball is way wide on the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A nasty one! Shorter in length, Ball takes his eyes off the ball and tries to fend. The ball takes the edge and goes towards third man for a run.
Jake Ball walks out to the middle.

OUT! Bairstow, what have you done? That was very soft. He has fallen straight into the trap. Two wickets in two overs for Starc. England are losing their way completely. Starc bangs it in again, Bairstow goes for the upper cut, he might have wanted to get it a little squarer but hits it straight down the throat of Handscomb at third man. Just before the tea break, Jonny has to walk back. The lead is now 168, England will need a lot more and they only have two wickets left.
Flatter on off, the batsman defends it off the back foot.
Tosses it up on off, Broad drives it to covers.
Drives it with the spin to the man at covers.
Fires it down the leg side, Broad goes for the flick but misses. Paine takes it one-handed and appeals but he is the only one appealing.
The short of a length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Flatter on off, Bairstow defends it off the back foot.
Nathan Lyon is back into the attack.
Punches the short ball through the off side for another three.
The batsman has stood up on his toes to play that one. One run added to the total.
Short and outside off, cut through point for three runs.
Starc spears a fast delivery, 144.2 kph, full and on middle. It tails back in a bit and Broad somehow keeps it out towards backward square leg. Smiles as he crosses for a run.
Stuart Broad is the next man in. They say that fast bowlers have elephant's memory. Starc must be remembering the send-off he got by Broad after getting out. Time for revenge?

OUT! The change of angle does the trick for Australia. It is a brute of a delivery to start with from around the wicket and you just can't keep the captain of the Australian team out of the game. Starc gets his first. He has not had the best of times with the ball but he has struck now. A good move by Smith as he just came into the second slip position prior to this ball. Starc bangs it short, as he has been doing. This one climbs onto the batsman. That is what the ball normally does here in Australia and hence it is difficult to stand and play. Woakes commits that mistake. He stands tall and tries to fend it. Gets surprised by the extra lift and has to leap to confront it. But the ball takes the shoulder of his bat and balloons to Smith who takes it safely. England are now seven down with the lead one short of 160.
Just short of a length on off, Bairstow flicks it towards mid on for a run.
Quicker on off, defended off the back foot.
Flighted ball on off, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Floats it on middle, Jonny gets it off the inner half through square leg for a run.
Very full outside off, the batsman drives it through covers for a run.
Tosses it up on off, Woakes defends it off the front foot.
Shortish again, Jonny sways away from the line of the delivery.
A quick short ball at 145 kph. Bairstow is late in his pull and the ball comes and hits the bat rather than the other way around.
Bangs it in short outside off, Woakes pushes it through covers for a run.
FOUR! A poor ball, should have been put away and it has been. Starc is just not at his best. He again bowls it short and wide outside off. Woakes cuts it through point for a boundary.
Back of a length on off, Woakes defends it off the back foot.
He comes around the wicket and angles it in on off, Woakes defends it off the front foot.
A long hop on middle, the batsman pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
Errs in line and bowls it on the pads, Woakes flicks it down towards fine leg for a couple. The lead is now 150, England would somehow look to add another 50.
Tosses it up on off, Woakes presses forward and drives it to covers.
Shorter in length on off, Woakes defends it off the back foot.
Drives the full ball to covers.
Floats it on middle, Woakes defends it off the front foot.

Risky! Bangs it in short on middle, Bairstow at the very last moment tries to play an upper cut but gets beaten. A risky shot by him. Also Starc has some words to tell him, though he does not respond.
Back of a length on off, Jonny defends it off the back foot.
Shorter in length this time, a well-directed one. Bairstow ducks under it.
Shorter in length outside off, Bairstow lets it be.
Back of a length on off, Jonny pushed it through cover-point. Some good running helped them take two.
Full ball on off, Bairstow drives it to covers.
Eases it down through mid off to retain strike.
Gives it air on off, Woakes drives it down to long off for a run.
Flatter on middle, Woakes defends it off the back foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Better by Smith! He tosses it up on off, gets it to drift into the batsman. Woakes defends it off the front foot.
Short ball outside off, Bairstow cuts it through point for a run.
Steven Smith now comes into the attack. We saw Joe Root taking a wicket yesterday. Can he do the same?
Fullish ball on off, Woakes drives it to the man at mid off.
Fires it down the leg side, Woakes misses the flick and it goes through to the keeper.
Bowls it on a length outside off, the batsman opts not to play at it.
Shorter in length outside off, Woakes does not play at it.
NO BALL! Wide outside off, too wide actually. He has also overstepped. Woakes opts not to play at it.
Good length on off, Chris defends it off the front foot.
Length ball outside off, Woakes lets it be.
Mitchell Starc is back into the attack.
Floats it on middle, Woakes works it around the corner for a run.
Flicks it with the spin through square leg for a run.
Driven towards the mid on region. They pick up a single.

Almost a chance! Flatter on middle, Woakes tries to work it on the leg side. He does so uppishly but straight to Bancroft who at short leg does not sway away from the ball. Keeps his eyes on the ball but still fails to catch. Anyway, good work from the debutant.
Shorter in length outside off, Jonny cuts it towards point for a run. The runs have dried up here. They have only scored 10 runs after Moeen Ali's wicket.
Drives the full ball to mid off.
Close to the edge! Short and outside off, stays a touch low. Woakes tries to pull but is beaten by the low bounce.
Just short of a length on off, Woakes pushes it to covers.
A leg slip in place now.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Back of a length on off, Woakes defends it off the back foot.
On the pads, Bairstow gets an inside edge as he tries to flick. The ball rolls towards the leg side for a run.
Shorter in length outside off, Jonny cuts it to point.
Pushes it off the back foot through covers for no runs.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Quicker on middle, Woakes camps back and defends it.
Pushes it through covers for a run.
Tosses it up on off, Jonny defends it off the front foot.
Flatter on middle, turns into the batsman. Bairstow tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. There is an appeal from the bowler but then he pulls out of it.
Good length on off, Woakes defends it off the front foot.
FOUR! Excellent shot by Woakes! Hazlewood bowls it fuller on middle, gets it to reverse into the batsmen. Chris walks across and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary. England now lead by 136.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Shorter in length on off, Woakes defends it off the back foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Good length on off, Woakes defends it off the front foot.
Drinks!

Flatter on middle, turning back in. Bairstow tries to flick but misses and the ball strikes him on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head again. This was surely missing leg. An action-packed over comes to an end.

Was that pad first or bat first? Shane Warne on-air feels it is pad and he is disappointed with the fact that Australia did not review. They do have two reviews up their sleeves. Coming to the delivery - Lyon bowls it flatter on off and gets it to turn back in. Bairstow tries to defend with his bat close to the pads. The Australians appeal and the umpire stays put. What did it hit first? Replays later on show that it was pad first. It would have been very close had Smith reviewed. He should have taken a chance there. Hang on, hang on... a good decision in the end by Steven as later on Hawk Eye shows it is going over the stumps. It seems that Steven Smith knew something that we didn't. My colleague from behind quietly says - It's the ground reality.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Driven towards the mid off region for no runs.
Flicks it with the spin this time to the man at mid-wicket.
Tries to flick it with the  spin. Bairstow misses and gets hit on the pads.
Shorter in length on off, gets big on the batsman. Woakes tries to defend but the ball hits him on the gloves and goes on the bounce to the slip fielder.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

He comes running in by hiding the ball in his hands. He might not want to show which side is the shinny one. It was on the right side as it could be seen as the ball was delivered. He errs in line though and angles it down the leg side. The batsman goes for the flick but misses.
Good length on off, straightens after pitching. Woakes plays inside the line only to get beaten.
Jonny has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Jumps out of the crease, gets beaten in flight but luckily his pads come in the way.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Woakes has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
DROPPED! A tough chance! Woakes flicks it with the spin, and he does it firmly towards short leg who cannot hang on to the catch. The ball rolls towards square leg for a run. These catches stick.
Gets back and punches it wide of mid off for a single.
Length outside off, Woakes lets it through to the keeper.
Flicks it through square leg for a run.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.
BOUNCER! The batsman ducks under it.
Fuller in length on off, the batsman drives it to mid off.
Length on off, Jonny defends it off the front foot.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
The batsman has been beaten by the off spin.
Comes down the track and drives it back to the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Chris Woakes walks out to the middle.

OUT! No, he has not! Lovely camera work there! That was very marginal. A huge breakthrough for Australia, just as a partnership was forming, Lyon gets the breakthrough. He now has all three left-handers in this innings. Lyon tosses it up on off and gets it to turn away sharply. Moeen Ali plants his front foot forward in defense but gets beaten. Paine collects the ball and whips the bails off quickly and appeals, he's quite confident. Moeen, although is seen shaking his head. They go upstairs, replays are not very conclusive. The third umpire wanted a better shot, a more squarer angle perhaps. He had a look at various angles and then finally decides to give it out after the masterpiece angle which hinted that nothing is behind the popping crease. The decision is made and Moeen has been given the marching orders. He is looking dejected on his way back. Michael Clarke on-air mentions the benefit of the doubt should have been given to Moeen Ali there after watching the stump camera angle as he felt Ali had something behind the line. A very, very marginal call, could have gone both ways. A big wicket nevertheless for Australia and now England are 6 down for a lead of 129. Also, this is the first time Moeen Ali has been stumped out in Test cricket.

Stumping appeal! They have gone upstairs. A brilliant delivery by Lyon to beat Moeen. Paine is quick to take the bails off and is pretty confident in his appeal. Does Moeen has his feet behind the line?
Flatter on off, turning away. Moeen prods forward and defends it.

Michael Clarke opines on air that Josh Hazlewood was either too full or too short in the first innings. But he has been a lot better in the second innings, more accurate, pace has been good and he's getting the ball to move in and out. Ian Healy, however, feels that Josh is still searching for consistency and continues to look into the areas where he wants to land the ball.
Cuts the short ball towards deep point and bags a brace.

Bowls the ball outside off, he was bringing it in all this time and then throws this one outside off. Bairstow goes for a loose shot away from his body but gets beaten. Hazlewood also has a word with him. Excellent over!
Good length on off, swinging back in. The batsman drives it back at the bowler only to hit the stumps at the non-striker's end.
Back of a length on off, Jonny plays it to point.
Fuller on off, tailing back in. A similar ball to the delivery which dismissed Joe Root. Bairstow played it much better as he drove it down towards mid off.
Fuller in length on off, Jonny drives it to covers.
Josh Hazlewood is back into the attack. Interesting he did not start after the break as he had taken Root's wicket just before it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Bairstow flicks it with the spin through square leg for a run.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
BEAUTY! Lyon tosses it up on middle, the ball turns away sharply. Ali lunges forward and tries to defend but gets beaten.
Flatter on middle, Ali works it to mid-wicket.
Tosses it up outside off, spins away further. Moeen lets it be.
Good length on off, Jonny guides it to gully.
Back of a length on off, Jonny pushes it to mid off.
On the pads, Ali flicks it down to deep square leg to change strike. Poor by Cummins, all his fielders were on the off side and he drifted it on the pads.
Both of them are busy players and runs will keep ticking if they are at the crease. Once again, Bairstow flicks it with the angle through square leg for a run to bring up the 150.
Back of a length on off, the batsman defends it off the back foot.
Shorter in length on middle, Jonny ducks under it.
Flicks it with the spin through the leg side for a run.

SIX! First six of this innings! We know Bairstow is a dangerous stroke maker and he just shows why. Lyon floats it up on middle, Jonny makes good use of his feet to get to the pitch of the ball and lofts it over the mid-wicket boundary for a maximum. The lead is now above 120.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Flatter on middle, Ali gets well back in his crease and flicks it towards wide mid on for a run.
Shorter in length on off, Ali punches it to covers.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Short on the body of the batsman. Ali pulls it down to fine leg for a run.
Slower ball on off, Ali reads it well and defends it off the front foot.
Strokes it through the off side for a run.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Flicks it off his pads to the man at deep square leg for a run.
Full toss on off, Ali pushes it to covers.
Tosses it up on off, Jonny prods forward in defense.

FOUR! Too easy as there is no one in the cover region! Lyon bowls it way outside off, Bairstow strokes it through covers. Cummins gives it a chase but is not able to stop it. He nearly hurt his knees there on the slide, needs to be careful.
Flatter on off, Bairstow lunges forward and blocks it.
Works it against the spin towards wide mid on for a run.
Shorter in length on off, Ali punches it to covers.
Flatter on middle, Ali covers the line and defends it.
Good length on off, Jonny defends it off the back foot.
Length on off, pushed to covers.
Back of a length on off, Bairstow pushes it down to mid off.
BOUNCER! Bairstow ducks under it.
Fuller ball on off, the batsman drives it to mid off.
Length on off, Jonny defends it off the front foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Why is there no short leg? Maybe because Moeen is playing attacking cricket. Well if there was one, Ali could have been a goner. Smith has missed a trick here. Quicker on middle, goes on with the arm. Ali tries to defend but it takes the inside edge, hits the pads and goes uppishly through the vacant short leg area towards square leg.
Flatter on off, Ali defends it off the back foot.
Tosses it up on off, Ali lunges forward in defense.
Wide enough for the batsman to play at it.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Errs in line and angles it on the pads, Jonny flicks it down towards fine leg. Hazlewood there runs to his right and saves a couple for his side.
Shorter in length on middle, Jonny watches it early and ducks under it.
FOUR! Third boundary after the lunch break! Short ball outside off by Cummins. Bairstow cuts it through point for a boundary.
Bowls it on the pads, Bairstow tries to flick but gets an inside edge onto his pads. There is a muted appeal from the Australians but nothing from the umpire.
Flicks it with the angle to the man at square leg.
Length on off, Jonny defends it off the front foot.
Pat Cummins will bowl from the other end.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
FOUR! Nails the sweep to perfection this time! Fuller in length from Lyon, Mooen goes down on one knee and sweeps it through square leg for a boundary. The lead has now crossed 100.
Drags his length back outside off, Ali cuts it to covers.
FOUR! Top shot! Good intent from Moeen, he should not let Lyon dictate terms here. He sees flight on the delivery and comes down the track to loft it over mid on for a boundary.
BEATEN! Tosses it up on off, turns away sharply! Ali tries to defend but gets beaten.
Wide outside off, Ali lets it be.
We are back for the second session. Moeen Ali and Jonny Bairstow will continue their innings. Nathan Lyon will continue his spell.
...Day 4, Session 2...

The home side will hope for the same to continue after the break. They have their tails up and would look to wrap up the innings as quickly as possible. The visitors on the other hand have to show great fight and resilience and form partnerships if they are to come up with a competitive total. A lot of action still remains in the game. Do join us for the second session in a while.

Australia are right on top heading into the break! They have half the side back in the hut and the lead is still below hundred for England. Earlier in the morning, the away side came out with a positive intent and started to score freely. Runs were coming thick and fast for them until the introduction of Nathan Lyon which changed the course of the game. He weaved his magic and managed to pick two quick wickets and now with Root departing to Hazlewood the tourists are staring down the barrel.
Bouncer, around off, Jonny sways away from the line at the last moment. LUNCH ON DAY 4!
Width on offer outside off, Bairstow tries to run it down to third man but finds gully.
Pitches it full and on off, Moeen doesn't try to hit it hard and drives it down the ground past the bowler. The mid off fielder runs after it and slides to pull it back. A single taken.
Tight leave! Hazlewood angles across a length ball around off, moving away a shade, Moeen covers the line and makes brave leave.
Turns it in front of mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a single.
Good length ball on off, Bairstow remains on the back foot in defense.
Loopy and around off, spinning away, Moeen initially looks to push at it but then withdraws his bat.
Moeen has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Moeen is very severe on anything short. Lyon drops one in the middle of the pitch, Ali goes deep inside the crease and blasts his pull shot through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Flatter and on middle, Moeen goes on the back foot and punches it to the off side.
Full flighted ball on off, Ali lunges and defends it back.
Tossed up ball outside off, spinning away, Moeen allows it through.
Jonny Bairstow comes out to bat.

OUT! There goes the run-machine and England have half the side back in the hut. What a wicket for Australia! Mark Taylor at the start of the day's play did mention that Root is falling over too much while attempting to play it on the on side. He at that time brought out the clip of Joe's first innings' dismissal and pointed out his mistake. Root's head is falling over rather being nice and straight with eyes parallel to the ground and that has brought his downfall yet again. Falls prey to an inswinger by Hazlewood this time. Josh bowls a full length ball on off and gets it to tail back into the batsman. Root leans forward and across a bit too much as he tries to play on the leg side. He misses the ball completely and it hits him on the front pad. The Australians appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Root is dejected as he is walking back. He, then, stops and has a chat with Moeen but decides not to review it. A wicket on a lead of 87 which often is considered to be Australia's unlucky number but it's a myth as England have lost most wickets on the devil's number.

Fifty for Root! His 33rd in Tests! He is leading from the front here and has to do what Smith did yesterday, i.e. Bat for a long, long time. Josh bowls it on the pads, Root flicks it through mid-wicket for a brace. The crowd realizing that he has reached his fifty shouts ROOOOT. He raises his bat to acknowledge the applause.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Full ball on off, Ali drives it brilliantly through mid off for a boundary.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
The hammer is out to level out the bowling area! Nathan Lyon himself was a curator before and he would know what exactly is going on, quips Kevin Pietersen on air.
Flicks it against the spin towards square leg for a run.
Flatter outside off, Ali lets it be.
NO BALL! Comes down the track and flicks it down to long on for a run. There were three men behind square on the leg side and hence a no ball was called.
Sweeps it against the spin through square leg for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! 100 up for England! Runs started to come here for them! Ali errs in line and fires it down the leg side. Ali flicks it fine towards fine leg for a boundary.
Length on off, Root defends it off the front foot. 8 runs from the over and the lead is now 72.
FOUR! Second boundary from the over! Josh bowls it fuller in length on off, tailing back in. Root times his drive through mid off. Warner there, gives it a chase, and dives but all in vain.
Fuller in length on off, Root eases it to covers.
Fuller in length on middle, Root drives it down to mid on.
FOUR! Poor ball and dispatched! There were two fielders at backward point but Root still finds the gap. Short and wide outside off from Josh. Root cuts it through that region for a boundary.
He starts off with a length ball outside off, Root opts not to play at it.
Josh Hazlewood is back into the attack.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, too easy for Ali. He slaps it through covers for a boundary.
Floats it up on off, Ali defends it solidly.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tosses it up on off, Moeen covers the line and defends it.
Sweeps it with the spin towards fine leg for a run. Joe Root is looking to be proactive against Lyon which is a good ploy by the English skipper.
Too full on the pads, Ali flicks it towards wide mid on for a run.
Oh, no! He persists with short one and Moeen tucks it around the corner for a run.
Bangs it in again on leg stump. Ali ducks under it. Time for a yorker from Starc now?
Short again by Starc but this was nicely played by Moeen. He sways out of the way of the delivery, dropping his gloves.
A quick bouncer, a well-directed one this time. Ali, at the very last moment ducks under it.
Shortish ball down the leg side. Ali watchfully lets it through.
Shorter in length on middle, Ali ducks under it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tosses it up on middle, Root lets it turn and then plays it to mid-wicket.
Works it to mid-wicket with the turn.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Shorter in length outside off, Ali punches it through the off side for three.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! He has managed to get that really fine! Starc once again persists with the short ball on leg stump. Root pulls it very fine down the leg side, past the diving Paine for a boundary.
Short ball around off, Root first thought about pulling it but then pulled out. He was half committed on the shot and hence the ball hits him on the bat and falls just short of Starc.
On the pads, Ali flicks it towards square leg for a run. The lead is now 50.

JUST SHORT! Excellent effort by Smith! Short by Starc on middle, does not rise as much as expected. Ali tries to sway away but the ball hits the gloves and lobs towards the slip cordon. Smith at second slip, knowing the ball won't carry to first slip, puts in a full length dive but the ball lands just short of him.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Back of a length on off, Root defends it off the back foot.
Again some vicious turn and spin away from Ali. He just stands back inside the crease helplessly as it whizzes past the outside edge of his bat. Exceptional bowling by Nathan Lyon!
BEATEN! Welcome Moeen, says Lyon! He again tosses it up on off, the ball turns away sharply. Ali tries to defend but get beaten.
Moeen Ali walks out to the middle.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! It is the Lyon-Smith combination yet again! Brilliant from the off spinner, as mentioned he is the real dangerman and is living up to that tag. He once again gets the better of a left-hander. Tosses it up on middle and gets it to turn away. The ball also bounces a tad extra as Malan draws forward in defense. He seems to have the line covered but the away spin gathers the outside edge. Smith takes a relatively easier catch this time. He is having a picnic. Two quick wickets here and England are in deep trouble. Lyon roars in joy and England are now effectively 48 for 4. Prodding forward against Nathan is not a smart ploy, especially with the amount of spin and bounce he is getting, reckons Ian Chappell on air. Also, for the first time in a calendar year, Lyon has picked 50 wickets!
Slower through the air, Malan lets it be.
Shorter outside off, Malan punches it to covers.
Flatter on middle, turning into the batsman. Root flicks it down towards fine leg for a run. He is not getting it right to Root, he is bowling a better line to the left-hander.
Short ball on middle, Root pulls it towards fine leg. There is protection in the deep and the batsmen only get a single.
Starc switches to around the wicket! A similar angle in which he got Malan out in the first innings. He bangs it short but only bounces till waist height. Malan nudges it down to fine leg for a run.
Angles it on the pads, Root flicks it down to fine leg for a run. The lead is now 45.
On the shorter side outside off, Root cuts it to the man at gully.
Good length outside off, Root lets it be.
Shorter in length outside off, Root mistimes his cut to point.
Mitchell Starc is back into the attack. He has two men in the gully region and two slips also.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Shorter in length on middle, Root allows the ball to do its bit and then pulls it towards fine leg for a run.
Shorter in length outside off, Malan cuts it towards Khawaja at point, who dives to his left and makes a decent stop. Although, he cannot stop the single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
BEATEN! He has to get it a little fuller though! Flatter on middle, turns away from the batsman. Malan rocks back to defend but is beaten by the turn.
Works it around the corner with the spin for a run.
Good length on off, Root tries to defend but gets it off the inner half towards the leg side for a run.

Short ball by Cummins, Malan who also loves pulling the ball does so nicely towards backward square leg for a run. He has to be careful though as he fell prey to the short ball ploy in the first innings.
Length ball outside off, Malan watchfully makes a leave.
Angles it on the pads, Root flicks it but not off the middle towards square leg for a run.
Back of a length outside off, Root lets it be.
Angles in a good length ball on off, Root remains back and pushes it out with an angled bat to gully.
Wide enough for the batsman to leave it alone. Time for drinks!
Fires it in but on the shorter side. Malan camps back and defends it.
Root also dances down the track. Lyon pulls his length back a little seeing that. Joe adjusts and flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Makes good use of his feet and comes down the track. He drives it towards mid off and sets off for a run. The fielder there scores a direct hit at the striker's end but Root has made his crease.
Fuller on off, Malan defends it towards covers.
Flatter outside off, gets it to turn away further. Malan lets it be.
Bouncer down the leg side, Root as mentioned earlier does not like to duck much and goes for the pull but gets beaten.
Edged...but short! Good length on off, might have hit a crack. The ball straightens and takes the edge as he tries to defend. Falls short of Smith at second slip.
The batsman rocks onto the backfoot and punches the ball.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Back of a length outside off, Root punches it to the man at point.
Bouncer! Root ducks under it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Drags his length back outside off, Malan cuts it to point.
Dawid Malan strides out to the centre.

OUT! A big breakthrough for Australia this morning and Lyon is the man who provides it. He likes bowling to the left-handers and has delivered the goods. Stoneman, who looked rock solid out there, is walking back. Nathan tosses it up and lands on off, gets it to turn away with extra bounce. Stoneman plants his front foot ahead and tries to defend but it curves away to take the outside edge towards Smith at first slip. The Aussie skipper is very alert as always and goes down low to his left to complete a nice catch. The Australians are pumped up after a low profile beginning. This should get them going now. Forget the quickies, Lyon is the real dangerman. England are effectively 36 for 3.
Tosses it up on off, Stoneman drives it to covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter on middle, turning back in. Root camps back and plays it towards cover for a run.

That must have hurt! Stoneman since yesterday has dealt some blows! Cummins bangs in a short one, aimed at the rib cage of the batsman. Stoneman tries to leave it but gets hit on the back of the arm, just above the elbow to be precise.
Bouncer! Stoneman moves out of the way and lets it through to the keeper.
Flicks it with the angle through square leg to change strike.
Length outside off, Root defends it towards the off side for no runs.

Excellent bouncer! They have a field set for it. Cummins comes steaming in and bangs it short just outside off. Root tries to drag his pull but gets beaten in the process. A risky shot attempted by the skipper.
Just behind a length on off, Root defends it onto the ground.
Tries to bowl it quicker but on the shorter side. Mark camps back and defends it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Flatter on off, Stoneman defends it stoutly.
Gives it air this time on middle, Root flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Tucks it with the spin on the leg side.
Pitches it on leg stump, turning away. Root lets it be.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
FOUR! Just behind a length outside off, Stoneman punches it through backward point and gets a boundary. It goes uppishly past the right side of the gully fielder but safe in the end.
Fuller on the pads, Root flicks it towards wide mid on. Root called for two but had to settle for one.
Fuller in length on off, Root who is oozing with confidence today, plants his front foot ahead and drives it to the man at covers.
Back of a length on off, Root defends it towards mid on this time.
Good length on off, Root defends it to mid off.
Drags his length back outside off, Stoneman cuts it to point.
Fires it on middle, Stoneman defends it towards mid-wicket.
Bowls it quicker on middle, gets it to bounce a touch more. Stoneman defends it off the back foot.
Slower through the air on middle, turning away. Mark defends it solidly.
Quicker on off, Stoneman lets it turn away and then leaves it.
Flatter on off, Stoneman lunges forward in defense.

Spin early! Nathan Lyon is into the attack now from the Stanley Street End, the same end from where there's a crack starting to open up outside the right-hander's off stump. He is bowling to a left-hander at the moment and he loves that too. A slip and a short leg in place.
Much better! He bangs it in short on the body of Stoneman who tucks it around the corner for a run.
Yes we do but it is too wide outside off. Shorter in length, Stoneman lets it be.
A short leg in place along with a leg gully. He did trouble Stoneman with some short stuff yesterday. Will we see the same?
Back of a length outside off, Root off the back foot, punches it through covers for a run.
Good length on off, angling into the batsman. Root defends it onto the ground.
Back of a length outside off, Root defends it towards gully. He goes down and has a chat with his partner after playing the ball. They have come out really focused here.
Fullish ball on off, Root mistimes his drive towards mid off.
Pat Cummins is into the attack. He bowled a fiery spell yesterday. Australia will be expecting the same from him.
Back of a length on off, Stoneman hops and defends it onto the ground.
This time it is outside off, on the shorter side. Easy for Mark as he lets it through.
Errs in line, shorter in length. He is trying to get it at the body of Stoneman but has not found his rhythm yet. He bowls it down the leg side. Stoneman leaves it.
Shorter in length outside off, Root punches it through point for a run. He is a busy player once he gets going. He will keep ticking the scoreboard.
Just ahead of a length on the stumps, Stoneman pushes it towards wide mid on for a run.
Back of a length on off, Stoneman defends it solidly.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump. A maiden by Hazlewood.
Similar length outside off, Root cuts it towards Marsh at point who makes a good stop. Joe seems to be getting confident after each delivery he is facing.

Finds the edge but goes along the ground to gully! Good probing length from Josh. He bowls it around middle, straightens a touch, a similar delivery to what he bowled to Vince but that had a little more pace. Root gets squared up as he tries to defend it and gets a soft outside edge to gully.
Fullish on middle, Root eases it down to mid on.
Better by Hazlewood, he is now starting to find his length. He lands it around off. Root covers his off stump and lets it through.
Fuller in length outside off, Root lets it be.
Wide outside off, at 143 kph. Stoneman is not interested at playing at those.
Conventional length outside off, Stoneman shoulders his arms to it.
A better attempt of a short ball. He does get it to bounce a touch more but the line is down the leg side. Stoneman need not play at those.
Shorter outside off, no bounce off the wicket. Stoneman easily sways away from the delivery.
Length on middle, Root taps it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Angles it on the pads, Stoneman works it on the leg side for a run.
Fuller on the pads, too easy for Root. He clips it through mid-wicket for a couple.
FOUR! Runs are flowing today morning! Hazlewood bangs it short outside off, Root hops and guides it through backward point to fetch himself another boundary.

Another observation by Mark Taylor. On the fourth ball of the 17th over, Joe Root flicked one off the inner half. Taylor brought out the clip of his first innings' dismissal and points out his mistake. He reckons that Root's head is falling over rather being nice and straight with eyes parallel with the ground. Shane Warne adds to it and feels that Joe is a bit hesitant getting forward after copping a blow on the helmet yesterday evening. Fine details from the on air commentators.
Back of a length on off, Root guides it to gully.
Just ahead of a length on off, Root defends it off the front foot quite easily.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Good length on off, Root defends it solidly.

Here comes the short ball, but does not get up that much. Root as mentioned does not duck and goes for the pull. He does it well down towards fine leg for a run. Starc needs to get the ball to bounce a lot higher than the last one. That was a comfortable height for Root.
There are two men out for the hook shot. Joe Root doesn't duck too much, feels Mark Taylor on air. He is surprised that Mitchell Starc has not tested him so far with a short ball.
Back of a length on middle, Root camps back and defends it onto the ground.
Fuller in length on off, Root drives it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Elegant! Full and wide outside off, a juicy half-volley. Root leans into it and drives it through covers to give England their first boundary of the day.
A yorker again but outside off, Root once again digs it out to point.
Starts off with a yorker outside off, Root digs it out to covers.
Mitchell Starc to bowl from the Stanley Street End.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through. Four runs from the first over.
Length outside off, Stoneman lets it be.

Risky by Root, had he missed that he was plumb! His head is falling a little. Hazlewood bowls it a touch fuller on middle, Root plants his front foot across and tries to flick. He gets an inside edge through square leg for a single.

Root gets his first runs of the day as well! Pitched up ball on off by Josh, Root presses forward a bit, opens the face of the bat a little and guides it past the diving gully fielder. Good running by the batsmen to collect two.
Stoneman is away for today! Back of a length on middle by Hazlewood, Stoneman taps it towards mid on for a quick run.
He starts off with a length delivery in the zone outside off, a perfect Test match line. Stoneman watchfully allows it through to the keeper.

We are all set to get underway. Joe Root, the English skipper, and Mark Stoneman will continue their innings. A partnership is what is needed for England. They lead only by 7 at the moment. For Australia, Josh Hazlewood will start the proceedings. He has three slips and a gully in place. He already has two important scalps to his name. Can he provide an early breakthrough today? Let's find out. Here we go...

Joe Root has a big job in front of him. England will be hoping that he brings out his best game today and leads from the front. He still has a plenty of support left and constructing partnerships is the need of the hour. How will they fare against the hostile pace battery of Australia? Stay with us to find out...

Welcome, ladies and gentlemen. We witnessed the Steven Smith show yesterday where he scored an epic 141 not out to give Australia a slight lead. All this happened after the home side was reeling at one stage and that makes this century from their skipper very special and vital in the context of the game. After that, the Aussie speedsters got into the act last evening and it was a torrid time for the Englishmen. They are effectively 7/2 at this stage, under tremendous pressure but are still not out of the game in spite of the early damage.
...Day 4, Session 1...

Earlier in the day, England had the home side on the mat after bowling superbly in the first session. Australia were tottering on 209 for 7 but a valiant ton by skipper Steven Smith and his momentum changing 66-run partnership with Pat Cummins helped them gain a 26-run lead. They now have the game in their control and would want to continue the good work tomorrow, whereas the tourists would hope for Joe Root and the rest to battle it out and take them to a respectable total. We can expect another cracking day of Test match on day 4. Join us at 1000 local (0000 GMT) for all the action. You can now switch over to the India vs Sri Lanka second Test match where the hosts are in a dominating position. Cheers!

It was an exhibition of hostile bowling from the Aussie speedsters and that has put the hosts right on top heading into day 4! England lead by just 7 runs and are already two down. The Australian pacers bowled with good pace and maintained an excellent line to trouble the English top order. Josh Hazlewood bounced back from an ordinary bowling performance in the first innings and claimed both the wickets to fall. He was well supported by Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins from the other end, who were equally threatening.
Poor ball to end the day, just like Broad ended yesterday. Spinning down the leg side, Root lets it go through to the keeper. STUMPS ON DAY 3!

Brilliantly bowled, he finds the edge but to no avail! He gives it air on middle, gets it to turn away. Stoneman tries to defend with firm hands and gets an outside edge rolling towards short third man for a run.
Flicks it with the spin towards square leg for a run.
Tosses it up on middle, Root lunges forward in defense.
He is pushing it through but shorter in length outside off. Root pushes it to the man at covers.
Flatter outside off, turning back in. Root defends it off the back foot.
Just behind the length on off, Stoneman rocks back and defends it.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Back of a length on off, Stoneman camps back in defense.
Length ball on off, Root defends it towards covers for a run.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.

CLOSE! Quicker this time by Lyon, outside off at 95.5 kph, he wants it to go on with the arm and it does so. Stoneman opts not to play a shot at it and the ball goes really close past the off stump. Smart bowling!
Darts it on off, Stoneman punches it to the man at covers.
BEATEN! Floats it up on off, turning away. Stoneman lunges forward in defense but only to get beaten by the away turn.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Flatter on middle, Root flicks it through the leg side for a run.
Back of a length on off, Stoneman tries to defend but gets a soft outside edge towards the man at slip.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.

Stoneman is getting stoned here! Cummins again bangs it short on leg stump, Stoneman takes his eyes off the ball as he tries to fend at it. He takes one hand off the handle but the ball hits him on the glove which is holding the handle and rolls to leg gully. He is having a tough time here. This is hostile pace bowling.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

That is up in the air...but safe! Cummins is bowling really quick here. He bangs it short on leg stump, the ball comes quicker off the pitch. Stoneman tries to defend but the ball hits him on the glove and lobs way ahead of Khawaja who comes running in from gully.
Short but down the leg side, Stoneman lets it through to the keeper.

Lyon has not got it right in this over. He bowls it short again on middle, Stoneman camps back and times his flick through mid-wicket. Due to the big outfield here, the ball slows down as it gets close to the rope. Hazlewood comes running from deep backward square leg and picks up the ball. They take three and ENGLAND LEAD by the same margin!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Slower through the air on off, turns away after pitching. Stoneman tries to defend but is beaten by the away turn.
Flatter but on the shorter side by Lyon on middle. Stoneman flicks it to short leg.
SCORES LEVEL! Short ball down the leg side by Lyon. Root pulls it down towards fine leg for a run.
Drags his length back on middle, Root pushes it down to mid off.
Spin! Nathan Lyon is into the attack. A short leg, a leg slip and a slip in place.
Root is seen taking a medicine. Maybe for the blow he took on the head. He might be feeling a little dizzy after that.
Good length outside off, Mark lets it be. A maiden by Cummins to start off with.
Bangs it short on middle, Stoneman tucks it to short leg who was just brought in.
A short leg in place now.
Shorter in length outside off, Stoneman lets it be.
Full ball on off, Stoneman eases it to mid off.
Fuller in length outside off, Stoneman opts not to play at it.
Starts off with a beauty! He lands it on a length around off, gets it to shape away after pitching. Stoneman tries to defend but gets beaten.
Pat Cummins comes into the attack. He was extremely impressive in the first innings.
On a length around off, Root defends it off the back foot to mid off.
Full ball on off, Root drives it to mid off.
Fuller in length on off, Root times his drive well but it goes straight to point.
Good length on off, nipping back in. Root covers the swing and defends it back towards the bowler.
Bowls it on the pads, Stoneman flicks it down to fine leg for a run.
Bangs it in on off. Stoneman defends it off the back foot.
Angles it on the pads, Stoneman works it down to fine leg to keep strike.
Short aimed at the rib cage of the batsman. Root pulls it down to fine leg for a run.
Fuller this time outside off, Root opts not to play at it.
Good length on off, angling away. Root defends it by covering the line of the ball.
Short ball down the leg side, Root ducks under it.
Short and outside off, Root resists the temptation to cut and lets it through to the keeper.
Fullish ball on off, Mark drives it to mid on.
FOUR! A much-needed boundary for England! Fuller ball outside off by Hazlewood from around the wicket. Stoneman drives it through covers and the ball races to the fence.
Short ball outside off, does not bounce enough. Stoneman evades it.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Fuller in length this time on off, Stoneman defends it off the back foot.
Back of a length outside off, Stoneman plays inside the line and lets it through.
Good length outside off, Root lets it be.
Bouncer again and Root this time ducks under it.
The physio is out now to check whether Root is fine. Joe is having a sip of water and now it looks like he wants a change of helmet. He looks to be fine though, good news for the English fans.

Right on the helmet! Starc has his tail up here! He bowls it short and the ball skids off the surface. Root is late to react and tries to fend by taking his eyes off the ball. The ball hits him straight onto the helmet. Good gesture by the Australians as they walk up to the English skipper to ask him whether he is fine.
Back of a length on off, Root defends it with authority off the back foot.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Flicks the ball on the pads down to fine leg for a run.
Similar length on off, Root defends it solidly.
Back of a length on off, Root defends it off the back foot.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Joe Root comes out to the middle. He will have to replicate what Smith did for Australia.

OUT! Second one down and Josh Hazlewood is breathing fire here! Look what one wicket does, he has an extra yard of pace in his deliveries and is also getting the ball to move. He lands it on a length around middle and off and gets it to nip away a touch. James is not sure whether to play forward or back. Ends up trying to defend from the crease but gets squared up. It catches the edge of his bat and goes to second slip where Smith pouches it. He edged the ball prior to this also but it didn't carry to the fielders in the slip cordon. England are in big trouble here. They have already two batsmen back in the hut and are yet to wipe off the deficit. The top scorer for England in the first innings departs early.
Edged but short! Josh bowls it on a length around off, shapes away off the seam. Vince tries to defend but gets an outside edge which falls just short of third slip.
Good bowling, he is now oozing with confidence here Hazlewood. He lands it on a length around off, gets it to move away. Vince first thinks of playing at it but then lets it go.
Loose very loose from Stoneman. Starc serves a full ball outside off, inviting the batsman to drive. Stoneman obliges and goes for it but away from his body. He gets beaten.
Back of a length on middle, Stoneman defends it off the back foot.
Flicks it with the angle to mid-wicket.
Absolute gem of a delivery! He goes wide of the crease and lands it on off, gets it to shape away after pitching. Stoneman tries to defend but gets beaten.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
FOUR! Too easy for Stoneman! Starc dishes out a full ball on leg stump, Stoneman flicks it through square leg and the ball races to the fence.
On the pads, Vince flicks it through backward square leg for a couple.
He bends his back on that one and bowls it short on leg stump. Vince ducks under it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
James Vince walks out to the middle. He impressed one and all in the first innings. England would hope he repeats the same.

OUT! Hazlewood strikes and the Gabba erupts! Another failure for Cook courtesy a very good catch by Starc at fine leg. Hazlewood bangs it short on leg stump. Cook tries to pull but fails to middle it properly. He gets a top edge and it flies towards Starc. He runs across to his left and bends low to take a brilliant catch. An early wicket for Australia, just what they needed. Also Hazlewood gets a wicket, this should get him going now. It does mean a lot to him which shows in his celebration. England trail by 15. Cook was troubled many times by the short ball ploy in the 2013-14 Ashes and he falls prey to one today. Big blow to England.
Wide outside off, Cook need not play at it.
Back of a length on off, Cook defends it off the back foot.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Nice bounce and pace there by Starc! 146 kph! He bangs it short and wide outside off, Stoneman tries to cut but gets beaten by the extra lift that the ball got off the surface.
Back of a length on off, Cook taps it towards covers for a run.
EDGY FOUR! Cook won't mind though! Starc lands it on a length around off. Cook tries to defend but it takes an outside edge through gully for a boundary.
Shorter in length but on the leg stump. Cook flicks it through square leg for a brace to get off the mark.
Flicks it with the angle to square leg.
Just ahead of a length on off, the batsman defends it.
Bowls it on a length outside off, Stoneman opts not to fiddle with it. This also zips off the surface and also gets good carry as it reaches Tim Paine.
A better line and length! He lands it on off, getting it to angle away. Mark defends it off the front foot.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Good length outside off, Stoneman lets it be.
FOUR! A boundary to get off the mark for Stoneman! Short and wide outside off by Hazlewood. Stoneman cuts it uppishly but wide of the point fielder.
Josh Hazlewood will bowl from the other end. He did not have a good outing with the ball in the first innings but he has a chance to make amends.
Back of a length on off, Cook defends it to point. A maiden to start off by Starc.
Fuller in length on off, Cook mistimes his drive to mid on.
Length ball on off, no swing available for Starc. Cook defends it solidly.
Good length on off, Cook defends it off the front foot.
Length outside off, Cook lets it be.

Action straightaway! Not the best of balls as he sprays it down the leg side. Cook tries to flick but misses and the ball goes off something to the keeper who takes it and appeals. The umpire shakes his head. Replays later on show it had flicked the pad. Cook will be disappointed to not hit that away.
